Gardens everlasting which they shall enter, streams running beneath, theirs then shall be whatsoever they will. Thus does Allah recompense those who fear Him.
Those whom the angels take away while they are goodly, saying: peace be upon you, enter the Garden for what you have been working.
Do they await that the angels should come to them or the Command of your Rabb should come? Thus did those before them. Allah wronged them not, but they were used to wrong themselves.
Then there befell them the vices of what they had worked, and then surrounded them that at which they had been mocking.

And those who associate say: had Allah willed we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither our fathers; nor would we have forbidden anything apart from Him. This did those before them. Nothing is then on the Messengers excepting a plain preaching.

And assuredly We have raised in every community a Messenger saying: worship Allah and avoid the devil. Then of them were some whom Allah guided, and of them were some upon whom the straying was justified. So travel about the land and behold how has been the end of the beliers.
If you are solicitous for their guidance, then verily Allah does not guide whom He sends astray and for them there are no helpers.
They swear by Allah the most solemn of oaths that Allah would not raise him who dies. Yea! It is a promise on Him incumbent, but most men know not.
This will be in order that He may manifest to them that wherein they differ, and that those who disbelieved should come to know that they had been liars.
Our only saying unto a thing, when We intend it, is that We say to it: Be; and it becomes.
And those who have emigrated for the sake of Allah after they had been wronged, We will surely settle them well in the world, and the wage of the Ākhirah is greater, if they but knew.
They are those who bear in patience, and in their Rabb they trust.
And We sent not before you any but men to whom We Revealed; so ask you the people of the Admonition if you know not.
We sent them with evidences and Scriptures. And We have sent down unto you the Admonition that you may expound unto mankind what has been revealed towards them and that haply they may reflect.
Do then those who have plotted vices feel secure that Allah will not sink them into the earth or that the torment may come from whence they know not?
Or, that He will not seize them in their going to and fro? So that they cannot escape.
Or, that He will not seize them by giving them a fright? Verily your Rabb is Kind, Merciful.
Have they not observed the things Allah has created? Shadows thereof turn themselves on the right and the left bowing themselves before Allah, and they are lowly.
And before Allah bows itself whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth of the living creatures and also the angels; and they are not stiff-necked.
They fear their Rabb above them and do what they are commanded.
Allah has said: take not you to two gods; He is only one God. So dread Me, Me Alone.
His is whatsoever is in the heavens and the earth, and unto Him obedience is due perpetually; will you then fear any other than Allah?
And whatsoever of favours is with you is from Allah; then when distress afflicts you, to Him you cry out.
Then when He removes the distress from you, forthwith a party of you associates others with their Rabb.
That they may show ingratitude for what We have bestowed upon them. Enjoy then, presently you shall know.
And they appoint for what they know not a portion of what We have provided them. By Allah! You shall surely be questioned regarding what you have been fabricating.
And they appoint for Allah daughters – Hallowed be He! And for themselves what they desire.
And when there is announced unto any of them a female, his face remains darkened the whole day and is wroth inwardly.
Sulking from the people because of the evil of what has been announced unto him: shall he keep it with ignominy or bury it in the dust? Lo! Vile is what they judge!
For those who are disbelievers in the Akhirah is an evil similitude. And for Allah is the sublime similitude, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

And if Allah were to seize mankind for their wrongdoing, not a living creature He would leave on it, but He defers them to an hour and when their hour comes they cannot delay it a moment nor anticipate it.
They ascribe to Allah what they detest, and their tongues utter the falsehood that unto them shall be good; undoubtedly unto them shall be the Fire, and they shall be hastened thereto.
By Allah! We have sent Messengers to communities before you, then Satan made their own works seem fair to them, so he is their patron today and to them shall be a torment afflictive.
And We have not sent down the Book to you save in order that you may expound to them that whereon they differ, and as a guidance and Mercy to a people who believe.
Allah has sent down from the heaven water, then He revives the earth by it after its death; verily in that is a Sign for a people who listen.
Verily there is a lesson for you in the cattle; We give you to drink of what is in their bellies, between the dung and blood: milk, pure and pleasant to swallow for the drinkers.
And also a lesson is for you in the fruits of date palms and the grapes of which you take a liquor and a goodly provision, verily in that is a Sign for a people who understand.
And your Rabb inspired the bee saying: take you for yourself houses of hills, of trees, and of what they erect.

Then eat you of all manner of fruits and tread the ways of your Rabb made easy. There springs forth from their bellies a drink varied in colours; in it is a healing for mankind; verily in that is a Sign for a people who reflect.
Allah has created you; then He takes your souls. Of you are some who are brought back to the meanest of age, so that they know not anything after having knowledge; verily Allah is Knowing, Wise.

And Allah has preferred some of you over some others in provision; then those who are preferred are not going to hand over their provision to those whom their right hands possess, so as to be their equal in that respect. Do they then deny the Favour of Allah?

Allah has made for you of yourselves spouses, and from your spouses He has made for you sons and grandsons; and He has provided you with clean foods. Do they then believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah's Favour?
And they worship, besides Allah, what does not and cannot own for them any provision from the heavens and the earth.
Do not propound then similitudes for Allah; verily Allah Knows and you do not.

Allah Propounds a similitude: there is a bondman enslaved who has not power over anything, and there is one whom We have provided from Ourselves with goodly provision and he spends out of it in private and public; can they be equal? Praise be to Allah. But most of them do not know.

And Allah propounds a similitude: there are two men, one of them dumb who has no power over anything, and is a burden to his master, wherever he despatches him he brings to him no good; is he equal to him who commands justice and is himself on the straight path?
Allah's is the Unseen of the heavens and the earth, and the affair of the Hour will be not but as a flash of the eye. Or it is even nearer, verily Allah is over everything Potent.
And Allah has brought you forth from the bellies of your mothers while you know not anything, and He appointed for you hearing and sight and hearts that perchance you might give thanks.
Do they not see the birds subjected in the firmament of the heaven? None supports them save Allah; verily there are Signs in that for a people who believe.

Allah has made for you from your houses a repose, and He has made for you from the skins of your cattle houses which you find light on the day of your flitting and on the day of your stopping, and from their wools and their furs and their hair a furnishing and an enjoyment for a season.

And Allah has made for you of what He has created shades; and He has made for you from the mountains places of retreat, and He has made for you coats protecting you from the heat and coats protecting from the violence. Thus He perfects His Favour on you that perhaps you may submit.
Then if they turn away from you, on you is only a plain preaching.
They recognize the Favour of Allah, yet they deny it, and most of them are infidels.
Beware a Day whereon We will raise up from each community a witness, then those who have disbelieved shall not be given leave, nor shall they be permitted to please Allah.
And when those who have done wrong will see the torment, it shall not be lightened unto them, nor shall they be respited.

And when those who have associated will see their associate-gods, they will say: O our Rabb! Yonder are our associate-gods upon whom we have been calling besides You; they will proffer them the saying: verily you are liars.
And they will proffer submission to Allah on that Day, and there will stray from them what they have been fabricating.
Those who disbelieved and hindered others from the way of Allah – We will increase for them torment upon torment for they have been spreading corruption.

And beware a Day whereon We shall raise up in every community a witness from amongst themselves regarding them, and We shall bring you as a witness regarding these. And We have Revealed unto you the Book as an exposition of everything, and as guidance and Mercy and glad tidings to the Muslims.
Verily Allah Commands justice and well doing and giving to kindred; and He prohibits lewdness and wickedness and oppression. He exhorts you that per chance you may be admonished.
Fulfil the Covenant of Allah when you have covenanted, and do not break oaths after their confirmation and surely you have appointed Allah your surety. Surely Allah Knows whatever you do.

And do not be like her who unravels her yam into strands after its strength, holding your oaths a means of discord amongst you that a community may be more numerous than another community. Allah only tests you thereby, and He will surely show to you on the Day of Judgment that wherein you have been differing.
Had Allah so willed, He would have made you all one community, but He sends astray whom He will and guides whom He will; and certainly you will be questioned about what you have been working.

And do not make your oaths a means of discord against you lest a foot may slip after its fixture, and you may taste evil for having hindered others from the way of Allah, and for you there shall be a torment mighty.
And do not barter the covenant of Allah for a small price; verily what is with Allah – is better for you, if you only know.
Whatever is with you is exhaustible, and whatever is with Allah is lasting. And we will surely recompense those who have been patient, their wage for the best of what they have been working.
Whoever works righteously, male or female, and is a believer, We will surely quicken him to a clean life, and will surely recompense them their wage for the best of what they have been working.
And when you would read the Qurān, seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the damned.
Verily he has no authority over those who believe and have trust in their Rabb.
His authority is only over those who befriend him and those who are in respect of Him associators.
Whenever We change a verse in place of another verse – and Allah is the Best Knower of what He sends down – they say: you are but an impostor. Aye! Most of them know not.
Say you: the Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Rabb with truth, that it may establish those who believe, and as guidance and glad tidings to the Muslims.
And assuredly We Know that they say: it is only a human being who teaches him. The speech of him to whom they incline is foreign, while this is plain Arabic speech.
Verily those who do not believe in the Signs of Allah - Allah shall not guide them, and to them there shall be a torment afflictive.
It is only those who do not believe in the Signs of Allah who fabricate a lie, and those! They are the liars.

Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief – save him who is constrained and his heart is at rest with the belief – but whoever expands his breast to unbelief, upon them shall be wrath from Allah and to them shall be a torment mighty.
That is because they loved the life of the world above the Ākhirah, and because Allah does not guide an infidel people.
These are they upon whose hearts and hearing and sight Allah has set a seal; and these! They are the heedless!
Undoubtedly in the Hereafter they shall be the very losers.
Then, verily, your Rabb unto those who emigrated after they had been persuaded, and have thereafter striven hard and endured – your Rabb is thereafter. Forgiving. Merciful.
Beware of a Day whereon every soul will come pleading for itself, and every soul will be paid in full what it has wrought, and they shall not be wronged.

Allah propounds a similitude: a town which was secure and at rest, to which came its provisions abundantly from every place; then it denied ungratefully the favours of Allah; therefore Allah made it taste the extreme of hunger and fear, because of what they were used to perform.
And assuredly there came to them a Messenger from amongst them, but they belied him, wherefore Our torment seized them, while yet they were wrongdoers.
So eat of what Allah has provided you of lawful and clean things, and give thanks for Allah's Favour, if it is He Whom you are used to worship.

He has disallowed to you only the dead-meat and blood and swine-flesh and that over which is invoked the name of other than Allah; then whosoever is driven by necessity, not lusting nor transgressing, verily Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.
And do not say concerning that wherein your tongues utter a lie: this is allowed and this is forbidden, that you may forge a lie against Allah; those who forge a lie against Allah shall not prosper.
A passing enjoyment; and then unto them shall be a torment afflictive.
To those who are Judaised We had forbidden what We have already recounted unto you; and We wronged them not, but themselves they were used to wrong.
Then, verily your Rabb unto those who work evil from ignorance and then repent and amend – your Rabb thereafter is to such Forgiving, Merciful.
Verily Ibrahim was a pattern of piety, devout unto Allah, upright, and was not of the associators.
Grateful for His Favours: He chose him and guided him to a straight path.
And We granted to him good in this world, and in the Hereafter he shall be of the righteous.
We Revealed afterwards unto you: follow you the faith of Ibrahim the upright; and he was not of the associators.
The Sabbath was prescribed only for those who differed thereon, and your Rabb will decide between them on the Day of Judgement concerning that wherein they differed.

Call you to the way of your Rabb with wisdom and goodly exhortation, and argue with them with what is best. Verily your Rabb! He is the best Knower of him who has strayed from His way, and He is the Best Knower of the guided ones.
And if you chastise, then chastise with the like of what you were chastised with, and if you endure patiently then surely it is better for the patient.
And endure them patiently, and your patience is not but from Allah; and do not grieve over them, and do not you be in straitness because of what they plot.
Allah is with those who are in awe of Him and those who are well doers.

Hallowed be He! Who carried His bondman in a night from the Masjid al Ḥarām to the Masjid al Aqṣā, the environs of which We have blessed, that We might show him of Our Signs! Verily He! He is the Hearer, the Beholder.
And We gave Mūsa the Book and made it a guidance to the Children of Isrāīl: take not beside Me a Guardian.
O progeny of those whom We bore with Nūḥ! Verily he was a bondman grateful.
And We decreed for the Children of Isrāīl in the Book: you shall surely commit evil twice in the land and you shall rise very high.
Then when the Promise came for the first of the two, We raised against you bondsmen of Ours endued with great violence, so they entered the dwellings; and it was a Promise fulfilled.
Thereafter We gave you a return of victory over them and We supported you with riches and children, and We made you a numerous concourse.

If you will do well you do well for yourselves; and if you will do evil, you shall sin against your own selves. Then when the second Promise came, We raised up a people that they may disgrace your faces and may enter the Mosque even as they entered it the first time, and that they may destroy with utter destruction whatever may fall under their power.
Perchance your Rabb may yet have Mercy on you; and if you still revert, We will revert likewise. And We have appointed Hell a prison for the infidels.
Verily this Qurān guides unto that path which is straightest and bears glad tidings to the believers who work righteous deeds that theirs shall be great wage.
And that those who do not believe in the Ākhirah - for them We have prepared an afflictive torment.
And man prays for evil as he should pray for good, and man is ever hasty.

And We have appointed the night and the day as two Signs; then We detailed the Signs of the night and made the Signs of the day illuminating that you may seek grace from your Rabb, and that you may know the number of years and the reckoning; and everything We have detailed in full.
And every man: We have fastened his actions round his neck, and We shall bring forth unto him on the Day of Judgment a book preferred him open.
Read your book; suffices today your soul against you as a reckoner.

Whoever is guided, it is only for himself that he is guided, and whoever strays it is only against his soul that he strays; and not one laden bears the load of another. And We do not chastise until We have raised a Messenger.
And when We intend that We shall destroy a town We Command its affluent inhabitants, then they transgress therein, and thus the word is justified on them. Then We annihilate it completely.
And many a generation We have destroyed after Nūḥ. And suffices your Rabb, the Aware, the Beholder, for the offences of His bondsmen.
Whoever intends the quick-passing world We hasten to him therein whatever We please to whom We intend; thereafter We shall appoint for him Hell where he shall roast, reproved, damned.
And whoever intends the Hereafter and strives therefore with due striving while he is a believer, then those! Their striving shall be appreciated.
To each – these and those – We extend the bestowal of your Rabb, and the bestowal of your Rabb is never restrained.
See you! How We have preferred some of them over some others; and surely the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preferment.
Set not up along with Allah another god, lest you sit down reproved, renounced.

And your Rabb has decreed that you should worship none but Him, and show kindness to parents; and if either of them or both of them attain old age with you, say not unto them: pooh! And browbeat them not, and speak to them a respectful speech. And your Rabb has decreed that you should worship none but Him, and show kindness to parents; and if either of them or both of them attain old age with you, say not unto them: pooh! And browbeat them not, and speak to them a respectful speech.

And lower unto them the wing of meekness out of Mercy, and say: Rabb! Have Mercy on both as they brought me up when young. And lower unto them the wing of meekness out of Mercy, and say: Rabb! Have Mercy on both as they brought me up when young.

Your Rabb is the Best Knower of what is in your souls; if you have been righteous, then He is unto you Penitent, Forgiving. Your Rabb is the Best Knower of what is in your souls; if you have been righteous, then He is unto you Penitent, Forgiving.

And give you to the kinsman his due, and also to the needy and wayfarer; and squander not in squandering. And give to the kinsman his due, and also to the needy and wayfarer, and squander not in squandering.
Truly the squanderers are the brothers of the devils, and the Devil is ever ungrateful to his Rabb. Truly the squanderers are the brothers of the devils, and the Devil is ever ungrateful to his Rabb.

And if you turn away from them awaiting a Mercy from your Rabb which you hope, then speak to them a gentle word. And if you turn away from them awaiting a Mercy from your Rabb which you hope, then speak to them a gentle word.

Let not your hand be chained to your neck, nor stretch it forth to its extremity, lest you sit down reproached, impoverished. Let not your hand be chained to your neck, nor stretch it forth to its extremity, lest you sit down reproached, impoverished.

Verily your Rabb extends the provisions for whom He Will, and measures it out: He is in respect of His creatures Aware, Beholder. Verily your Rabb extends the provisions for whom He Will, and measures it out; He is in respect of His creatures Aware, Beholder.
Kill not your offspring for fear of want: We provide for them and for yourselves; their killing is a great crime.
And do not approach adultery; it is ever an abomination and vile as a pathway.

And do not kill anyone whom Allah has forbidden except by right, and whoever is killed wrongfully, We have surely given his next of kin authority; so let him not exceed in killing; verily he is ever succoured.
And do not approach the substance of an orphan save with what is best, until he reaches the age of strength. And fulfil the covenant; verily the covenant shall be questioned about.
And give full measures when you measure, and weigh with an even balance, that is good, and the best interpretation.
And do not you go after that of which you have no knowledge. Verily the hearing and the sight and the hearts, each of them shall be questioned about.
And do not you walk on the earth struttingly; verily you will not by any means rend the earth, nor can you attain the mountains in stature.
Each of these! The vice thereof is to your Rabb ever detestable.
That is part of that wisdom which your Rabb has revealed to you, and set not up you along with Allah another god, lest you be cast into Hell reproved, damned.
Has then your Rabb distinguished yourselves with sons and taken for Himself the females from amongst the angels? Verily you say a saying.
Assuredly We have propounded it variously in this Qurān so that they might be admonished; but it adds only to their aversion.
Say you: were there along with Him other gods, as they assert, then they would have brought a way to the Owner of the Throne.
Hallowed be He, and exalted be He above what they say – a great height!

There hallows Him the seven heavens and the earth and whoever is therein. And nothing there is but hallows His Praise, but you do not understand their hallowing. Verily He is ever Forbearing, Forgiving.
And when you recite the Qurān, We set up between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a curtain drawn down.
And We set up veils over their hearts lest they understand it, and in their ears heaviness; and when you mention your Rabb Alone in reciting the Qurān, they turn back as averter.
We are the Best Knower of that motive with which they listen to you and whenever they counsel together in secret, when the wrongdoers say, you but follow a man enchanted.
See! How they propound similitudes for you. They have strayed away and cannot find a way.
And they say: when we shall have become bones and fragments, shall we in truth be raised as new creation?
Say you: become you stone or iron.

Or anything created of the things more remote in your breasts. Then they will say: who will restore us? Say you: He Who created you the first time. Then they will wag their heads at you, and say: when will it be? Say you: perhaps it is near.
The Day whereon He will call you, and you will answer with His Praise, and you will imagine that you had stayed but little.
Tell you My servants that they should say only what is best. Satan would stir up strife among them; Satan is to man ever an open foe.
Your Rabb is the Best Knower of you, He will have Mercy upon you if He Wills, or He will chastise you if He Wills. And We have not sent you over them as a trustee.
And your Rabb is the Best Knower of those who are in the heavens and the earth. And assuredly We have preferred some Prophets over some others, and We gave Daūd a Scripture.
Say you: call upon those whom you fancy beside Him; they are able neither to remove the distress from you nor to change it.

Those whom they call upon seek access themselves to their Rabb, striving which of them shall be the nearest; and they hope for His Mercy and fear His Chastisement; the Chastisement of your Rabb is indeed ever to be guarded against.
Not a town is there but We are going to destroy it before the Day of Judgment, or to chastise it with a severe chastising; that is inscribed in the Book.
And nothing hinders Us from sending the Signs except that the ancients belied them. And We gave to Thamūd a she-camel as an illumination, but they did her wrong. And We send not Signs but to warn.

Recall when We said to you: your Rabb has encompassed mankind. And We made the vision We showed you but a temptation for man, and likewise the tree accursed in the Qurān. And We warn them, but it only increases their exorbitance greatly.
And recall when We said to the angels: bow down before Adam. So they bowed, but Iblīs did not; he said: shall I bow to one whom You have created of clay?
Iblīs said: bethink You: this one whom You have honoured above me? If You defer me till the Day of Judgment, I will surely seize his progeny save a few.
Allah said: be you gone; whoever of them follows you, Hell is your requital, an ample requital.

And unsettle them whoever of them you can with your voice, and summon against them your horse and your foot, share with them riches and children and make promise to them, and Satan promises not but to delude.
Over my bondsmen you have no authority, and your Rabb suffices as a Guardian.
Your Rabb is He Who speeds for you the ship in the sea that you may seek His Grace; verily He is to you ever Merciful.
And when there touches you a distress on the sea, those you call upon fall away except He Alone, then when He delivers you on the land you turn away, and man is ever ungrateful.
Are you then secure that He will not cause a side of land to swallow you up, or send over you a sand storm, and then you will not find for yourselves a protector?

Or, are you secure that He will not send you back therein another time and send upon you a gale of wind and drown you for your having disbelieved, so that you will not find for yourselves an avenger against Us?

And assuredly We have honoured the Children of Ādam, and have borne them on the land and the sea, and We have provided them with clean things, and We have preferred them with a preferment over many of them whom We have created.
Remember the Day when We shall call all mankind with their record; then whoever will be given the book in his right hand — those will read their book, and they shall not be wronged a whit.
And whoever has been blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter and far astray from the path.
And surely they had nearly tempted you away from what We have Revealed to you, that you should fabricate regarding Us something else, and then surely they would have taken you as a friend!
And were it not that We had confirmed you had almost leaned towards them a little.
In that case, We would have surely made you taste the double of the torment of life and the double of the torment of death and then you would not find a helper against Us.
And surely they had almost unsettled you from the land that they might drive you forth from hence. And in that case they would not have stayed after you but a little while.
This was Our dispensation with those whom We sent before you of Our Messengers and you will not find a change in this Our dispensation.
Establish the Şalāt from the declination of the sun to the darkening of the night and the recitation at the dawn; verily the recitation at the dawn is ever borne witness to.
And of the night keep the vigil therein as an act of supererogation for you; perchance your Rabb will raise you up in a station Praised.
And say you: Rabb! Cause me to enter a rightful entrance and cause me to go forth a rightful outgoing, and appoint for me from before You a helpful authority.
And say you: the truth has come and falsehood is vanished: verily falsehood is ever vanishing.
And We reveal by means of the Qurān what is a healing and a Mercy to the believers; and it only increases the ungodly in loss.
And when We show favour to man, he turns away and withdraws on his side; and when evil touches him, he is ever despairing.
Say you: everyone works after his disposition, and your Rabb is the Best Knower of him who is best guided on the path.
And they ask you regarding the Ruh. Say you: it is only the Command of my Rabb, and of knowledge you have been given only a little.
And if We willed, We could surely take away what We have revealed to you, then you will not find against Us any protector.
Except as a Mercy from Rabb, verily His Grace unto you is ever great.
Say you: if the mankind and the Jinn leagued together that they might produce the like of this Quran, they could not produce its like, though one to the other were a backer.
And assuredly We have variously propounded all manner of similitudes in this Quran for the mankind, yet most men have refused everything except disbelief.
And they say: we will by no means believe in you until you cause a fountain to gush forth for us from the earth.
Or there be for you a garden of palms and vines and you cause rivers to gush forth in their midst.
Or you cause the sky to fall upon us, as you assert, in pieces, or you bring Allah and the angels face to face with us.

Or there be for you a house of gold, or you mount to the sky, and we will by no means believe even in your mounting until you cause a book to be sent down to us which we may read. Say you: hallowed be my Rabb! I am nothing but a human being sent as a Messenger.
And nothing has prevented men from believing when the guidance came to them except that they said: has Allah sent forth a human being as Messenger?
Say you: were there on the earth angels walking about contentedly. We would certainly have sent down to them an angel from the heaven as a Messenger.
Say you: Allah suffices as a witness between me and you; verily He is in respect of His creatures ever the Aware, the Beholder.

And whom Allah guides he is the rightly guided, and whom He sends astray – for such you will by no means find friends beside Him. And We shall muster them on the Day of Judgment lying prone, blind, deaf and dumb, their abode being Hell. As soon as it grows dull, We will increase the Flame for them.
This shall be their return because they disbelieved in Our Signs and said: when once we have become bones and fragments, shall we in truth be raised up a new creation?

Do they not see that Allah Who created the heavens and the earth is able to create their likes? And He has appointed for them a term of which there is no doubt; yet the ungodly have rejected everything except infidelity.
Say you: if it were you who owned the treasurers of the Mercy of my Rabb, you would surely refrain from spending for fear, and man is ever miserly.
And assuredly We gave Mūsa nine manifest Signs – ask you the Children of Isrāīl – so when he came to them, the Pharaoh said to him: I imagine you to be spell bound, O Mūsa!
Mūsa said: assuredly you know that none has sent down these things save the Rabb of the heavens and the earth as an enlightenment, and verily I imagine you doomed, O Pharaoh.
Then he sought to scan them out of the land; therefore We drowned him and those with him, all together.
And after him, We said to the Children of Isrāīl: dwell on the earth; then when comes the promise of the Ākhirah, We shall assemble you all together.
And with truth We have sent down the Qurān, and with truth it has come down, and We have not sent you but as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner.
And this is a Recitation which We have made distinct that you may recite it to mankind with slow deliberation and We have revealed it at intervals.
Say you: whether you believe it or believe it not, verily those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down on their chins, prostrating.
And they say: Hallowed be our Rabb! The Promise of our Rabb was ever to have been fulfilled.
And they fall down on their chins weeping, and it adds to their humility.
Say you: call upon Allah or call upon Rahmān, by whichsoever name you call, His are the Excellent Names. And shout not your prayer, nor speak it low, but seek a midway.
And say you: all praise is to Allah Who has not taken a son, and Whose is no associate in the dominion, nor has He a protector through weakness, and magnify Him with all magnificence.
All praise to Allah Who has sent down to His bondman the Book, and allowed no crookedness therein.
Straightforward, that it may warn of a severe violence from before Him, and bring glad tidings to the believers who work righteous works that theirs shall be a goodly wage.
They will abide there forever.
And that it may warn those who say: Allah has taken a son.
No knowledge they have of it, nor had their fathers. Odious is the word that comes from their mouths; they utter not but a lie.
You are, as if going to kill yourself over their footsteps out of sorrow for they do not believe in this discourse.
We have made whatever is on the earth as an adornment of it, that We test them – which of them is best in work.
And We are going to make whatsoever is on it a bare soil.
Do you think that the people of the cave and the inscription were of Our Signs a marvel?
Recall when the youths took themselves to the cave and said: O our Rabb! Grant to us Mercy from before You and prepare for us in our affair a right course.
Therefore We put a covering over their ears in the cave for a number of years.
Thereafter We raised them up that We might know which of the two parties was best at reckoning the time that they had tarried.
We recount to you their tidings with truth. They were certain youths who believed in their Rabb, and We increased them in guidance.
We braced their hearts when they stood forth and said: our Rabb is the Rabb of the heavens and the earth; never we shall call upon a god beside Him, for then we shall be saying an abomination.
These, our people, have taken for themselves gods beside Him why then do they not bring for them a clear authority? Who does a great wrong than he, who fabricates a lie against Allah?

And now when you have withdrawn yourselves from them and what they worship, except Allah, take yourselves to the cave; your Rabb will unfold for you some of His Mercy, and will prepare an easy arrangement of your affair for you.

And you would see the rising sun veering away from their cave on the right, and the setting sun passing them on the left, while they were in the spacious part of the cave; that is of the Signs of Allah. Whom Allah guides, he is the guided indeed, and whom He sends astray, for him you will never find a directing friend.

And you would have deemed them awake whereas they were asleep, and We turned them over on the right and the left, while their dog stretched forth his two fore legs on the threshold. Had you looked at them you would have surely turned away from them in fright and would have been filled with awe of them.

Likewise We raised them up that they might question among themselves. There spoke a speaker from amongst them: how long have you stayed? They said: we have stayed a day or part of a day. They said: your Rabb knows best how long you have stayed; now send one of you with this your money in the city, and let him find which food is the cleaner there, and let him bring you a provision for that, and let him be circumspect, and let him by no means discover you to anyone.
Verily they, if they come to know of you, would stone you or make you revert to their faith, and lo! Then you shall never fare well.

And likewise We caused their affair to be lit upon that they might realise that Allah's Promise is true, and that the Hour! There is no doubt about it. Recall when they were disputing among themselves regarding their affair, and then they said: build over them a building – their Rabb is the Best Knower about them – then those who prevailed in their affair said: surely we shall raise over them a place of worship.

Presently they will say: they were three, the fourth being their dog. And they will say: they were five, the sixth being their dog – guessing at the unknown – and they will say: they were seven, the eighth being their dog. Say you: my Rabb is the best knower of their number; none knows that except only a few; so debate not you regarding their number except an outward debating, and ask not anyone regarding them.
And never say you of a thing: I am going to do that on the morning.
Except with this reservation that Allah so will. And remember your Rabb when you forget, and say you: perchance my Rabb will guide me to something nearer to right direction than this.
And they stayed in their cave three hundred years and added nine.

Say you: Allah knows best how long they stayed; His alone is the hidden knowledge of the heavens and the earth. How well He sees and hears! They have no patron beside Him, nor in His Rule He associates anyone.
And recite you what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Rabb; and none may alter His Words, and never will you find beside Him a refuge.

And endure yourself in the company of those who call upon their Rabb in the morning and evening seeking His Countenance, and let not your eyes rove from them seeking the adornment of the life of this world; and obey you not him whose heart We have made to neglect of Our remembrance, and who follows his lust, and whose affair is exceeding the bound.

Say you: the truth is from your Rabb, let him therefore believe who will and let him disbelieve who will. Verily We have prepared for the wrong doers a Fire the awnings of which shall encompass them; and if they cry for relief they shall be relieved with water like the dregs of oil scalding their faces. Ill the drink, and vile the resort!
Verily those who believe and work the righteous works We do not waste the wage of him who does well in regard to his work.

These! For them are the Gardens Everlasting with running streams. Bedecked they shall be therein with bracelets of gold and wear they shall green robes of satin and brocade, reclining therein on the couches. Excellent the reward, and goodly the resort!
Proclaim to them the similitude of two men. We made for one of them two gardens of vines and hedged both with palms, and We placed tillage in between.
Each of the two gardens brought forth the produce, and stinted not anything thereof, and We made stream to gush forth in the midst of the two.
And he had property. Then he said to his companion as he spoke to him: I am better than you in substance and mightier in respect of retinue.
And he entered his garden, while he was a wrong doer in respect of his own soul. And he said: I do not consider that it will ever perish.
Nor I consider that the Hour is going to happen; and if I am brought back to my Rabb, surely I shall find something better than this as a retreat.
His companion said to him; as he spoke to him: are you a disbeliever in Him who created you of dust; then of a sperm, and formed you a man?
But, He is Allah, my Rabb, and with my Rabb I do not join anyone.
Why then you said not when you entered your garden: whatever Allah may will, there is no power save in Allah; if you see then I am inferior to you in substance and offspring.
Then perchance my Rabb will give me something better than your garden and send on it a bolt from the heaven so that it become a slippery plane.
Or the water thereof becomes deep sunken, so that you can make a search therefor.

And his property was encompassed, and lo! He was wringing the palms of his hands over what he had spent on it, so it lay fallen down on its trellises, saying: oh! Would that I had not joined anyone with my Rabb!
And there could be no party helping him as against Allah, nor could he be an avenger himself.
Herein is all protection from Allah the True; Excellent is He as to the reward and Excellent to the final end!

Propound you to them the similitude of the life of this world. It is as water which We send down from the heaven, then there mingles with it the vegetation of the earth, and lo! It becomes dry stubble, which the winds scatter. And Allah is Potent over everything.
Riches and sons are the adornment of the life of the world, and the righteous works that last are excellent with your Rabb in respect of reward and excellent in respect of hope.
And beware of a Day when We will cause the mountains to pass away, and you will see the earth plain, and We will gather them, and We will leave of them not one.
And they shall be sent before your Rabb in ranks. Now you have come to Us as We had created you the first time. Aye! You fancied that We had appointed for you no meeting place.

And the Book shall be placed, and you will see the culprits alarmed at what is therein, and they will say: ah! Woe to us! What ails this Book that it leaves not any misdeed, small or great, but it has comprehended it! And they shall find present all that they had wrought; and your Rabb wrongs not any one.

And recall when We said to the angels: do Sajdah to Ādam, and they did Sajdah, but Ibīs did not. He was of the Jinn, so he trespassed the command of his Rabb. Would you then take him and his progeny as patrons instead of Me, whereas they are unto you an enemy? Ill is for the wrong doers this exchange.
I made them not present at the creation of the heavens and the earth or at the creation of themselves; nor was I to take the seducers as supporters.
And beware a Day whereon I shall say: cry unto My associates whom you fancied. So they will call upon them and they will answer them not. We shall place between them a barrier.
And the culprits will see the Fire and imagine they are about to fall therein; and they shall not find therefrom a way of escape.
And assuredly We have set forth all manner of parables in this Qurān for mankind, but man is of all things the most contending.

And nothing prevents mankind from believing now when the guidance has come to them and from asking forgiveness of their Rabb, except that there may come to them the dispensation of the ancients or that the chastisement may come to them face to face.

And We do not send Messengers save as bringers of glad tidings and warners, and those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood that they may rebut thereby the truth; and they take My Signs and what they are warned of as a mockery.

And who does greater wrong than he who is admonished with the Signs of his Rabb and yet turns away from them and forgets what his hands had sent forth? We have set up veils over their hearts lest they should understand it, and in their ears a heaviness; and if you call them to the guidance, lo! They will not let themselves ever be guided.

And your Rabb is the Forgiver, Owner of Mercy. Were He to call them to account for what they have earned, He would have hastened torment for them, but for them there is a return, and beside it they cannot find a place to take themselves to.
And these cities! We destroyed them when they did wrong, and We had appointed a time for their destruction.
And recall when Mūsa said to his page: I shall not cease journeying until I reach the confluence of the two seas, or I shall go on for ages.
And when the two reached the confluence of the two, they forgot their fish, and it found its way into the sea freely.
And when the two had passed by, he said to his page: bring to us our breakfast we have indeed got toil from this journey of ours.
He said: look here! As we were proceeding to the rock I became unmindful of the fish and nothing but Satan made me forget to mention it to you, and it took marvellously its way into the sea.
Mūsa said: that is exactly what we have been seeking. Then they turned back on their footsteps, retracing.
Then the two found a bondman from Our own bondmen, on him We had bestowed a Mercy from before Us and him We had taught knowledge from Our Presence.
Mūsa said to him: shall I follow you that you may teach me of what you have been taught directive knowledge.
He said: verily you will not be able to have patience with me.
And how can you have patience over that which your knowledge does not encompass?
Mūsa said: you will find me, if Allah will, patient, and I shall not disobey you in any affair.
He said: well, if you would follow me, then do not question me of anything, until I begin to mention it myself.

Then the two journeyed together until when they embarked in a boat, he scuttled it. Mūsa said: have you scuttled it that you may drown the people thereof? Assuredly you have committed a thing grievous.
He said: did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?
Mūsa said: do not take me to task for what I forgot and do not impose hardship in my affair.
Then the two journeyed till when they met a boy, and he killed him. Mūsa said: Have you killed an innocent person not in return for a person? Assuredly you have committed a formidable thing.
He said: did I not tell you; you would not be able to have patience with me?
Mūsa said: if I question you regarding anything after this, abandon me; surely there has reached you an excuse from my side.

Then the two moved on, until when they came to the people of a city. They begged food from the citizens, but they refused to entertain the two. Then they found therein a wall about to collapse and he set it upright. Mūsa said: had you wished you could have taken a wage therefor.
He said: this shall be the parting between me and you. Now I shall declare to you interpretation of that over which you could have no patience.
As for the boat, it belonged to poor men working in the sea. I wanted to damage it, as was before them a prince confiscating every boat.
And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we apprehended that he might impose upon them exorbitance and infidelity.
So we intended that their Rabb should change for them one better than he in piety and closer in affection.

And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town and underneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father was righteous. So your Rabb intended that the twain should attain their maturity and bring forth for themselves their treasure as a Mercy from their Rabb; and I did it not of my own bidding. That is the interpretation of what you could not bear patiently.
And they question you of Zul Qamain. Say you: I shall recite to you some mention of him.
Verily We! We established him in the earth, and gave him the means of everything.
Thereafter he followed a way.

Until when he reached the setting place of the sun, he perceived it setting in miry spring, and he found a nation nearby it. We said: O Zul-Qamain! Either chastise them or take the way of kindness in respect of them.
He said: as for him who does wrong presently he shall chastise him, and then he shall be brought back to his Rabb, and He shall torment him with a formidable torment.
And as for him who believes and works righteously, for him will be a goodly wage, and soon we shall speak to him something easy of our affair.
Thereafter he followed a way.
Until when he reached the rising place of the sun, he perceived it rising upon a nation for whom We had not set a veil against it.
Thus it was. And surely We have encompassed in knowledge all that was with him.
Thereafter he followed a way.
Until when he arrived between the two mountains, he found beside them a people who almost did not understand a word.
They said: O Zul-Qarmain! Yajūj and Majūj are doing mischief in the land; should we then pay you tribute so that you place between us and them a barrier?
He said: better than your tribute is that wherein my Rabb has established me; so help me with your labour, and I shall place between you and them a rampart.
Bring me lumps of iron. Then when he had evened up the two mountainsides he said: blow! Then when he had made it a fire, he said: bring me molten copper and I shall pour it thereon.
In this way they were not able to scale it, nor were they able to burrow through it.
He said: this is a Mercy from my Rabb; then when the Promise of my Rabb comes, He shall make it powder, and the Promise of my Rabb is ever true.
And We will let them on that day, surge some of them against others, and the Trumpet shall be blown, and then We will muster together.
And We will set Hell on that Day unto the infidels with a setting.
Unto those whose eyes had been under a covering from My remembrance, nor had they been able to hear.
Do then who disbelieve think that they may take My bondmen instead of Me, as patrons? We have prepared Hell as an entertainment for the infidels.
Say you: shall I declare to you the greatest losers in respect of works?
They are those whose effort is wasted in the life of the world, and they imagine that they are doing well.
They are those who disbelieve in the Signs of their Rabb and in their meeting with Him, vain shall be made all their works, and We will not allow them any weight on the Day of Judgment.
That shall be their reward: Hell; for they disbelieved and held My Signs and My Messengers in mockery.
Verily those who believe and do righteous works, theirs shall be Gardens of Paradise for an entertainment.
Abiding therein, they shall not seek any removal out of them.
Say you: were the oceans to become ink for the words of my Rabb, these would surely exhaust before the words of my Rabb exhausted, even though We brought another ocean for support.

Say you: I am but a human being like yourselves; revealed unto me is that your God is One God. Whoever then hopes the meeting with his Rabb, let him do righteous deed, and let him not join anyone in the worship of his Rabb.
Kāf-Hā-Yā-'Ain-Ş'ad.
This is a mention of the Mercy of your Rabb to His bondman Zakariyya.
Recall when he cried unto his Rabb with a low tone.
He said: Rabb! My bones have waxen feeble and the head is glistening with hoariness, and I have not yet been in my prayer to You, my Rabb! unblessed.
And I fear my kindred after me, and my wife has been barren; so bestow on me from before You an heir.
Inheriting me and inheriting the Children of Ya'qūb, and make him, Rabb, acceptable.
O Zakariyya! We give you the glad tidings of a boy, and his name shall be Yahyā, We have not so far made his namesake in your family.
He said: Rabb! In what way shall there be a boy for me? My wife
Allah said: even so! Your Rabb says: it is to Me easy. Surely I have created you before, when you were not anything.
He said Rabb! Appoint me a Sign. Allah said: your Sign is that you shall not speak to mankind for three nights, while sound.
Then he came forth to his people from the sanctuary and he beckoned to them: hallow your Rabb morning and evening.
O Yaḥyā! Hold fast the Book. And We granted him wisdom, while yet a child.
And tenderness from Our Presence and purity, and he was pious.
And dutiful to his parents, and was not a highhanded rebel.
And peace be to him on the day of his birth and death, and on the day he will be raised up.
And mention you in the Book Maryam when she retired from her people to a place eastward.
Then she took beside them a curtain. Then We sent unto her Our Spirit, and he appeared to her in the form of a sound human being.
She said: Verily I take refuge with the Compassionate from you if you are God-fearing
He said I am but an envoy of your Rabb and have come to bestow on you a boy faultless.
She said how can there be a boy unto me, whereas no human being has touched me, nor have I been a harlot?
He said even so! Your Rabb says: easy it is with Me, and it is in order that We make him a Sign to mankind, and it is a Mercy from Us, and it is an affair decreed.
Then she concaved him, and she retired with him to a place far-off
Then the birth-pangs drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said: Would that I had died before this and had become forgotten, lost in oblivion.
Then one called from underneath her: grieve not; your Rabb has placed underneath you a rivulet.
And shake towards you the trunk of the palm-tree, dates will drop on you fresh and ripe.
So eat and drink you, and cool thine eyes, and if you see of humans anyone say you: Verily I have vowed to the Compassionate a fast, so I shall not speak to anyone today.
Then she brought the baby to her people carrying him. They said: O Maryam! You have brought a thing unheard of.
O sister of Harun: your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste.
Then she pointed to him. They said how can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a mere child?
He said: verily I am a bondman of Allah. He has given me the Book and made me a Prophet.
And He has made me blessed wherever I may be and enjoined on me Salat and purity as long as I am alive.
And dutiful to my mother, and not made me high handed and unblessed.
And peace be on me the day I was born and the day I die and the day I am raised up;
Such is 'Isa, son of Maryam; this is the word of truth, wherein they are doubting.
Allah is not one to take to Himself a son. Hallowed be He Whenever He decrees an affair, He only says to it Be, and it becomes.
And verily Allah is my Rabb and your Rabb, so worship Him, and this is a way straight.
Then the sects have differed among themselves, Woe to those who deny the witness of a mighty Day.
How wonderful in their hearing and in their sight will they be the Day they come to Us! But today the wrongdoers are in manifest error.
And warn them of the Day of Anguish when the affair shall have been decreed, while they are heedless and are not believing.
Verily We! We shall inherit the earth and whatever is thereon; and unto Us they shall be returned.
And mention you in the Book Ibrāhīm. He was a man of truth, a Prophet.
Recall when he said to his father: Father! Why do you worship that which neither sees nor hears, nor yet avails you at all?
Father! Verily there has come to me of knowledge what has not come to you; so follow me, and I shall guide you to an even path.
Father! Serve not Satan; surely Satan has been rebel against the Compassionate.
Father! Verily I fear there may touch you a torment from the Compassionate, as that you become a companion to Satan.
He said: Ibrāhīm! Are you averse to my gods? If you desist not, surely I will stone you, and depart you from me for ever so long.
Ibrāhīm said: peace be on you; presently I shall ask forgiveness for you from my Rabb; verily He is unto me ever solicitous.
And I renounce you and all that you serve besides Allah, and I shall call unto my Rabb, and I hope in calling unto my Rabb I shall not be unblessed.
Then when he had renounced them and all that they served besides Allah, We bestowed on him Ishāq and Ya'qūb and each one We made a Prophet.
And We bestowed on them of Our Mercy, and We made for them a lofty renown.
And mention you in the Book Musa; he was single-hearted, and was a Messenger, a Prophet.
And We cried unto him from the right side of the mount, and We drew him near for whispering.
We bestowed on him, out of Our Mercy, his brother Harūn, a Prophet.
And mention you in the Book Ismā'īl; he was true in promise, and was a Messenger, a Prophet.
And he used to bid his household to Şalāt and purity, and he was with his Rabb an approved one.
And mention you in the Book Idrīs. He was a man of truth, a Prophet.
And We exalted him to a lofty position.

These are they whom Allah has favoured from among the Prophets, of the progeny of Adam and of them whom We bore with Nūḥ and of the progeny of Ibrāhīm and Isrāīl, and of them whom We have guided and chosen. Whenever the Revelations of the Compassionate were rehearsed to them, they fell down prostrating themselves and weeping.
Then there succeeded them a posterity who neglected Şalāt and followed lusts; so they shall meet presently with the perdition.
Excepting those who may repent and believe and work righteously. These shall enter the Garden and shall not be wronged at all.
Gardens everlasting which the Compassionate has promised to His bondmen, though yet unseen; Verily His Promise is ever to be fulfilled,
They shall not hear therein any vain word, but they shall hear only peace; and they shall have therein their provision morning and evening.
Such is the Garden which We shall cause Our bondmen to inherit who have been God-fearing.
And we, the angels, do not descend, except by the Command of your Rabb. His is whatever is before us and whatsoever is behind us and whatsoever is in-between;" and your Rabb is never forgetful.
Rabb of the heavens and the earth and what is in-between; so Him worship you, and endure patiently in His worship; do you know any one as His competer?
And man says when I am dead, shall I be raised alive?
Does not man remember that We created him before he was anything?
By your Rabb, then We will surely gather them and the devils, thereafter We will surely bring them around Hell, kneeling.
Then We will surely draw aside from each sect those who were most rebellious against the Compassionate.
Then surely it is We Who know best as to which of them were the worthiest of being roasted therein.
And there is not one of you but shall pass over it, an ordinance decreed by your Rabb.
Then We will deliver them who kept from evil and will leave the wrong-doers kneeling therein.
And when Our clear Revelations are rehearsed to them, the infidels say to the faithful: which of the two portions is better in station and goodlier in company?
And how many a generation We have destroyed before them, who were goodlier in goods and outward appearance?

Say you; whosoever is in error surely unto him the Compassionate lengthens a length, until when they behold that with which they were threatened, either the torment or the Hour, then they shall have to know whosoever is worse in position and weaker in hosts.
Allah increases in guidance those who let themselves be guided; and with your Rabb the righteous works that last are excellent in respect of reward and in respect of return.
Have you observed him who disbelieves in Our Signs and says: surely I will be given riches and children.
Has he looked unto the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Compassionate?
By no means! We will write down what he says; and We will prolong for him the torment a length.
And We will inherit from him that of which he spoke and he shall come to Us alone.
And they have taken gods besides Allah that they might be a glory for them.
By no means! Presently they will deny their worship, and become an adversary unto them.
Do you not see that We have set the devils upon infidels inciting them by an incitement.
So hasten you not against them; We are only counting against them a counting.
On the day whereon We shall gather the pious unto the Compassionate as an embassy.
And shall drive the culprits to Hell as a herd.
They shall not own intercession, excepting those who have taken with the Compassionate a covenant.
And they say: the Compassionate has taken a son.
Assuredly you have brought a thing monstrous.
The heavens are well-nigh ren: and the earth cleft and the mountains fall in ruins.
That they should ascribe to the Compassionate a son.
It behoves not the Compassionate that He should take a son.
None there is in the heavens and the earth but must come to the Compassionate as a bondman.
Assuredly He has comprehended them and counted them a full counting.
And every one of them is to come to Him on the Day of Judgment alone.
Verily those who believe and do righteous works, the Compassionate will assign for them affection.
So We have made it easy in your tongue in order that you may thereby give glad tidings to the pious and warn thereby a people contentious.
And how many a generation We destroyed before them! But can you perceive anyone of them or hear of them even a whisper!
Taha
We have not sent down the Quran on you that you should be distressed.
But only as an admonition to him who fears.
A down-sent from Him Who has created the earth and the high heavens
The Compassionate Who on the Throne is established.
His is whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is on the earth and whatsoever is inbetween and whatsoever is underneath the earth.
And if you speak the word aloud, then He knows the secret and the most hidden.
Allah! No God is there but He. His are the Excellent Names.
Has there come to you the story of Mūsa?
Recall when he saw a fire and said to his family: stay you I have perceived a fire! Perhaps I may bring a brand from it for you, or I may find guidance at the fire.
Then when he came thereto, he was cried unto: O' Mūsa!
Verily I! I am your Rabb, so take off your shoes; you are in the holy valley, Tuwa!
And I! I have chosen you. So listen to what will be revealed.
And I! I am Allah. No God is there but I so worship Me and establish Şalāt for My remembrance.
Verily the Hour is coming. I wish to conceal it in order that every one may be recompensed according to what he has endeavoured.
So let him not who disbelieves in it and follows his own desire keep you away from it lest you perish.
And what is in your right hand, O’ Mūsa?
He said: it is my staff. I lean on it, and with it I beat down fodder for my sheep and for me there are other purposes in it.
Allah said: cast it down. O' Mūsa.
So he cast it down, and lo it was a serpent running along.
Allah said: seize it and have no fear. We shall restore it to its former state.
And press your hand to your side; it will come forth white, without hurt, as another Sign.
That We may show you of Our greater Signs.
Go you to the Pharaoh, he has grown exorbitant.
He said: Rabb! Expand for me my breast.
And ease for me my affair.
And loosen a knot from my tongue.
That they may understand my speech.
And appoint for me a minister from my household.
Harun, my brother.
Strengthen me through him.
And associate him in my affair.
That we may hallow You often.
And may make mention of You often.
Verily You! You are of us ever a Beholder.
Allah said: surely you are granted your petition, Mūsa!
And assuredly We conferred a benefit on you another time.
When We inspired to your mother what We inspired.

Saying: cast him in the ark, and cast him in the river, and the river will throw him on the bank, and then an enemy of mine and an enemy of his will take him up. And I cast on you love for Me, in order that you may be formed under My eye.

Recall when your sister was walking along and saying: 'Shall I direct you to one who will take care of him? Thus We returned you to your mother that she might cool her eyes and she might not grieve. And you slew a person, but We delivered you from sorrow, and We tried you with several trials. Then you tarried for years among the People of Madyan, then you came according to fate, Mūsa!
And I formed you for Myself.
Go you and your brother with My Signs and do not slacken in My remembrance.
Go you both to the Pharaoh; verily he has waxed insolent.
Then say to him a gentle saying: may he be admonished, or he may fear.
The two said: Rabb! We fear that he may hasten against us, or may wax insolent.
Allah said: fear not, verily I shall be with you both, Hearing and Seeing.

So go to him, and say: we are envoys of your Rabb, so let the Children of Isrāīl go with us, and do not chastise them; surely we have come to you with a Sign from your Rabb; and peace be upon him who follows the guidance.
Verily it has been revealed to us that the torment will be for him who denies and turns away.
The Pharaoh said: who is the Rabb of you both, Mūsa?
Mūsa said: our Rabb is He Who gave everything its existence, then guided.
He said: then what did happen to the former generations?
Mūsa said: that knowledge is with my Rabb in the Book; my Rabb neither errs nor forgets
Who has appointed for you the earth as a bed. And has opened for you the pathways in it, and has sent down from the sky water, and thereby We have brought forth all manner of plants.
Eat and pasture your cattle, therein are Signs for men of sagacity.
Of it We created you and to it We return you and from it We bring you forth once again.
And assuredly We showed him Our Signs, all of them, but he denied and rejected.
He said: have you come to us that you may drive us out of our land by your magic, Mūsa?
So we shall confront you with a like magic; so make between us and you an appointment in an open space, which we shall not fail, neither you.
Mūsa said: your appointment is the gala day. And that the people be gathered in the forenoon.
Then Pharaoh turned away, devised his stratagem and then he came.
Mūsa said to them: woe unto you! Fabricate not a lie against Allah, lest He extirpates you with a torment, and surely, he who fabricates, loses.
Then they wrangled about their affair among themselves and kept secret their private counsel.
They said: verily these two are magicians, intending to drive you forth from your land by their magic and to do away with your superior way.
So devise your stratagem and then come in a row. Fortunate today is he who overcomes.
They said: either you cast, or we shall be the first to cast.
He said: nay, cast you down. And lo! Their ropes and their staves, by the magic, made to appear to him as though they were running.
Then a sort of fear in his mind Mūsa felt.
We said: have no fear, verily you shall be the superior.
And cast you down what is in your right hand; it shall swallow up what they have wrought. They have only wrought a magician's stratagem, and the magician does not prosper wherever he comes.
Then the magicians were cast down prostrate. They said: now we believe in the Rabb of Mūsa and Harūn.

Pharaoh said: what did you believe in Him before I gave you leave? Surely he is your chief who taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and feet on the opposite sides; and will surely crucify you on the trunks of the palm-trees; and you will surely know which of us is sterner in torment and more lasting.

They said: we shall by no means prefer you over what has come to us of the evidences, and over Him Who has created us. So do decree you whatever you shall decree; you can decree only in respect of the life of this world.
Verily we! We have believed in our Rabb that He may forgive us our affairs, and also that to which you have constrained us in the way of magic. And Allah is the Best and Most Lasting.
Verily he who comes to his Rabb as a culprit, for him is Hell, in which he shall neither die nor live.
And he who comes to Him as a believer, and has done righteous deeds, then for them are high ranks.
Gardens everlasting with running streams, abiding therein; that is the reward for him who has purified himself.
And assuredly We revealed to Mūsa saying: depart with My bondmen in night, and trickle for them in the sea a dry path; you shall fear neither overtaking nor shall you be afraid.
Then the Pharaoh followed them with his hosts, and there came upon them of the sea what came upon them.
And the Pharaoh led his nation astray, and guided them not.
O Children of Isrāil! We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you on the right side of the mount and sent down on you Manna and Quails.
Saying: eat of the clean things with which We have provided you, and wax not insolent thereabout, lest My Wrath may come down upon you; and upon whom My Wrath comes down, he surely perishes.
And verily I am the Most Forgiving to him who repents and believes and works righteously and lets himself remain guided.
And what has made you hasten from your people, Musa?
Musa said: why. They are close on my footsteps, and I hastened to You, Rabb! That You might be well-pleased.
Allah said: verily We have tried your people after you, and Samri has led them astray.

Therefore, Mūsa returned to his people indignant and sorrowful. He said: my people! Did not my Rabb make to you an excellent promise? Did then the promise seem to you too long in coming? Or did you desire that the Wrath of your Rabb should come upon you, so that you failed to keep my appointment?
They said: we did not fail to keep your appointment of our own will, but we were laden with the load of the people's trinket, so we threw them, as did the Samri into the fire.
And he produced for them a calf, a body with a low. Then they said: this is your god and the god of Mūsa, and him he has forgotten.
Did they not see that it did not return a word to them, 'and owned for them neither hurt nor profit?
And assuredly Harūn had said to them afore. 'My people! You are only being tempted with it, and verily your Rabb is the Compassionate, so follow me and obey my command.
They said: We shall by no means cease to be assiduous to it until Mūsa comes back to us.
'Mūsa said: Harūn! What prevented you when you saw them going astray?
That you followed me not? 'Have you disobeyed my command?
Harūn said: my own brother! Hold me not by my beard nor by my head; really I feared that you would say: 'You have caused a division among the Children of Isrāil and have not kept my word.'
Mūsa said: What was your object, Samri?
He said: I saw what the people did not see. So I seized a handful of dust from the footstep of the angel, and then I cast it into the fire; thus my mind embellished the affair to me.

Mūsa said: be gone you! Verily it shall be yours in life to say: no contact, and verily yours is a tryst which you shall not fail. And look you at your god to which you have been devoted; we shall surely burn it, and scatter it in the sea in your presence.
Your God is only Allah, the One; other than Him there is no God. He Comprehends everything in knowledge.
Thus We recount to you some tidings of what has preceded; and surely We have given to you an admonition from before Us.
Whosoever turns away from it, verily they shall bear a burden on the Day of Judgement.
And they shall abide therein. It will be for them on the Day of Judgement as a load.
The Day when the Trumpet will be blown and We shall, on that Day, gather the guilty blear- cyed.
Muttering among themselves: you did not stay save ten days.
We very well know what they will say when the best of them in judgement will say: you did not stay save for a day.
And they question you regarding the mountains. Say you: my Rabb will scatter them with a total scattering.
Then He shall leave it a level plain.
In which you shall not find any crookedness or ruggedness.
That Day they shall follow the caller for whom there shall be no crookedness and voices shall be humbled for the Compassionate; so that you shall hear but muttering.
That Day intercession will not avail except him for whom the Compassionate gives leave, and of whom He approves the word.
He Alone knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot encompass it with their knowledge.
Downcast will be faces before the Living, the Self Subsisting, and disappointed will be he who bears a wrong.
Whosoever works of the righteous works and is a believer he will not fear wrong or be grudging.
And thus We have sent it down, an Arabic Recitation, and have propounded variously therein of the threats, that perhaps they may fear God, or that it may generate in them some admonition.
Exalted is Allah, the True King! Hasten you not with the Quran before its Revelation to you is finished, and say you: Rabb. give me increase in knowledge.
And assuredly We covenanted with Adam before, then he forgot. Indeed We did not find steadiness in him.
Recall when We said to the angels: seek obeisance to Adam. They sought obeisance, except Iblīs; he refused.
Then We said, Adam! Verily he is an enemy to you and your spouse, so let him not expel you twain from the Garden, lest you be distressed.
It is for you that you shall not hunger here nor go naked.
Nor that you shall thirst here nor shall suffer from the sun.
Then did Satan whisper to him, and said: Adam I shall direct you to a tree of eternity and a dominion that ages not.
Then the twain ate of that tree, so they beheld their nakedness, and they took to stitching upon themselves with leaves of the Garden. Thus did Adam disobey his Rabb, and erred.
Thereafter his Rabb accepted him, and relented toward him and guided him.

Allah said: get down you twain here from together. Some of you are an enemy to some others. Then if there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance, shall neither go astray nor be distressed.
And whoever turns away from My guidance, verily for him will be a shrunken livelihood, and We shall raise him up sightless on the Day of Judgment.
And he will say: Rabb! Why have You raised me sightless whereas I have been able to see?
Allah will say: in a like way did Our Signs come to you, and you ignored them, so you too shall be ignored this day.
We thus requite him who transgresses and does not believe in the Signs of your Rabb; and surely the torment of the Hereafter is most severe and most lasting.
Has it not served as guidance to them 'how many a generation We have destroyed before them, in whose dwellings they walk? Verily therein are Signs for men of reason.
And had not a word gone forth from your Rabb and a term determined, it must necessarily have come.
So bear you patiently with what they say, and hallow the praise of your Rabb before sunrise and before sunset, and hallow Him in parts of the night and the ends of the day, so that you be pleased.

And do not strain your eyes after what We have given pairs of them to enjoy: the splendour of the life of this world, that We might try them therein; and the provision of your Rabb is the best and most lasting.
And bid your household for Śalāt and persevere you therein. We do not ask any provision of you; it is We Who provide you. The happy end is for piety.
And they say: why does he not bring us a Sign from his Rabb? Has not there come to them the fulfilment of what is in the former Scriptures?
And had We destroyed them with a torment before it, they would have said: our Rabb! Why did You not send us a Messenger that we might have followed Your Signs before we were disgraced and humiliated?
Say you: everyone is on the watch; so watch on, and soon you shall know who are the fellows of the even path and who has let himself be guided.
Their reckoning has approached mankind, while they are turning away unheedingly.
No fresh admonition from their Rabb comes to them but they listen to it while they are sporting.
Their hearts being in a light mood. The wrongdoers keep secret their whispers among themselves: This is but a mortal like yourselves; what! Will you be affected by magic while you know?
The Prophet said: My Rabb knows the word in the heavens and the earth; and He is the Hearer, the Knower.
Aye! They say: a medley of dreams; aye! He has fabricated it, aye! He is a poet, so let him bring us a Sign, as the ancients were sent with.
Not a town which We destroyed before them came to believe: Will these believe?
And We sent not before you but human beings to whom We revealed; so ask the People of the Admonition if you do not know.
And We made them not bodies requiring no food, nor were they immortals.
Then We fulfilled to them the Promise, so We delivered them and those whom We Willed, and destroyed the extravagant.
And assuredly We have sent down to you a Book in which is admonition for you; will you then not reflect?
How many a town did We overthrow which were doing wrong, and We caused to grow up thereafter another nation!
Then when they perceived Our revenge, lo! They were from it fleeing.
Flee not, and return to that wherein you luxuriated and your dwellings, perhaps you will be questioned.
They said: Woe be to us, surely we have been wrong-doers.
And this ceased not to be their cry, until We made them a harvest reaped, extinguished.
And We created not the heavens and the earth and what is in-between in play.
Had We intended that We should choose a sport, surely We would choose it from before Us if We were going to do that.
Aye! We hurl truth against falsehood, so that it breaks it, and lo! It vanishes, and woe to you for what you utter!
His is whosoever is in the heavens and the earth and those near Him are not too proud to pay Him homage nor are they ever weary.
And they hallow Him night and day, they flag not.
Have they taken gods from the earth, who rise up the dead?
Had there been gods, besides Allah, in the twain, surely the twain could have gone to ruin. Hallowed be Allah, the Rabb of the Throne, from what they utter!
Questioned He shall be not as to what He does, while they shall be questioned.
Have they taken gods beside Him? Say you: Forth with your proof! This is an admonition to them with me and an admonition to those before me. But most of them know not the truth. So they are averters.
And We did not send any Messenger before you but We revealed to him: There is no god but Me, so worship Me.
And they say: The Compassionate has taken a son. Hallowed be He! Aye! They are bondmen.
They precede Him not in word, and by His Command they work.
He knows whatsoever is before them and whatsoever is behind them, and they intercede not except for him whom He approves. And in awe of Him they are fearful.
And whosoever of them should say: Verily I am a god beside Him, such a one We will requite with Hell. Thus We requite the ungodly.
Have not those who disbelieved considered that the heavens and the earth were closed up, and then We rent them? And We have made of water everything living. Will they not then believe?
And We have placed in the earth firm mountains lest it should move away with them, and We placed therein passages for paths, that perhaps they may be guided.
And We have made the heaven a roof, safe; and from the Signs thereof they are averters.
And He it is Who has created the night and the day, the sun and the moon, each in an orbit floating.
And We have not, before you, granted immortality to any human being, so if you pass away, are they to be immortals?
Every one is going to taste of death, and We shall try you with evil and good as a temptation, and to Us you will be returned.
And when the infidels look at you, they only take you up for mockery: Is this the one who mentions your gods with contempt? While in the mention of the Compassionate they are themselves blasphemers.
Man was created of haste. I shall surely show you My Signs, so ask Me not to hasten.
And they say: When is this torment coming, if you say the truth?
If the disbelievers only know of the time when, they shall not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces nor from their backs nor shall they be succoured!
Aye! It would come upon them on a sudden and will dumbfound them; they shall not be able to avert it, nor shall they be respited.
And assuredly mocked were the Messengers before you, then there surrounded the scoffers what they had been mocking at.
Say you: Who guards you from the Compassionate by night and day? And yet they avert themselves from the remembrance of their Rabb.
Have they gods who defend them against Us? They have no power to succour themselves; and against Us they cannot be kept company with.
Aye! We let these people and their fathers enjoy until there grow long upon them the life. Observe they not that We come upon their land, diminishing it by its borders?! Will they then triumph?
Say you: I only warn you by the Revelation; and the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
And if only a breath of the torment of your Rabb were to touch them, they will cry: Woe to us! We have been the wrong-doers.
